newsitem.title: UK: Softs Outlook-Coffee stays focus,sugar may edge up.
newsitem.headline: Softs Outlook-Coffee stays focus,sugar may edge up.

text.p: Robusta coffee should once again occupy the dominant position on London's soft commodity markets this week, although white sugar has room to push higher amid fears of supply tightness.

Coffee started Monday with a hefty downward correction after the dazzling rally seen last week, but traders said any setbacks could still be temporary and not alter the market's current strong bullish tone.
With supplies still tight and stocks at 20-year lows, the onset of the Brazilian winter would help underpin sentiment well through the frost period to mid-September.
Analysts said that while the market would be prone to hefty bouts of profit-taking, the overall uptrend would remain intact -- especially if there were frost fears.
According to independent forecaster Weather Services Corp, no damaging cold is expected this week in Brazil's coffee areas.
Technically, both London and New York are overbought and while a correction is long overdue, analysts said prices were showing few signs of a sustained reversal.
"The current bullish scenario has not changed at all. We are looking for higher levels still," said one trader.

But London opened sharply lower on Monday after a frantic bout of speculator selling hammered July arabicas by 12 percent on Friday in what the CSCE said was coffee's largest one-day decline on record.
"I think one can start asking questions about whether that's the end of the bull market later," said Adrian Haylor, an analyst at Sucden.

In white sugar, concern over seasonal tightness has prompted a persistent buying stream in recent weeks as the market is fearful of reduced supply between the tail-end of the European crop and the new 1997/98 campaign.
Traders said the firmness on the whites was expected to continue, making both the August/October spread and nearby arbitrage attractive buys.
"The whites are steady...and it's going to carry on being steady. All the trade are buying it," said one.
"You've got a supply problem for the August and I don't think that's going to change. You've got to be long of the spread and be long of the whites in general."

But with New York's key July raws contract expected to ease as funds move out of the position and Brazilians price sugars from around 11.30 cents/lb, the arbitrage should widen further from its current level of $75.

In cocoa, although fundamentals have remained broadly unchanged, traders said encouraging technical signs were emerging after the benchmark July contract finally cracked stiff initial resistance near 1,035 stg.
Cocoa's improved technical outlook was also attracting some short-term fund money, traders said.
After coffee's steep rally in both the London and New York markets, traders said some funds were taking profits and opting to invest in the less-overbought cocoa market.
July gapped up at Friday's open from Thursday's high of 1,033 stg to Friday's low of 1,036 and reached the highest level since April 29.
Its next resistance point was pegged at 1,050, one stg above the April 29 high. Technical analysts projected an eventual move to about 1,200 stg if July pierced 1,050.
